summary: Mikio Otsuki specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. In 2007, he is attested as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji and a professor at Hanazono University.

Mikisaburo Mori was a scholar of philosophy and sinology who studied at Kyoto University and Osaka University (literature doctorate, 1962). He held posts at Kyoto University, Osaka High School, Osaka University (1950, 1966–1973), and Bukkyo University (~1973–1980).
Milman Parry (1902–1935) was a linguist who studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet. He later served on the faculty at Harvard University from ~1929 to 1935.

Milo Cleveland Beach is an art historian and Indologist educated at Harvard College and Harvard University. His career included posts at the Fogg Museum, Williams College, the Smithsonian Institution, and as director of the National Museum of Asian Art (~1988–2001).

Milton Singer (1912–1994) worked in Indology and religious studies. After studying at the University of Texas at Austin and the University of Chicago, he served on the faculty at the University of Chicago from ~1940 to 1979.

Min Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who completed postgraduate studies at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005–2006). In 2026, he is attested as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Min Ling Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Min Thu Wun (1909–2004) was a linguist and scholar who studied at the University of Rangoon under Pe Maung Tin (~1930–1935) and later pursued studies at the University of Oxford (~1936–1939).
Minakshi Banerjee is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Debarchana Sarkar. In 2026, she held a James Prinsep Research Fellowship at The Asiatic Society.
Ming Chen is a scholar of Indology, sinology, and Buddhist studies who has served as a professor at Peking University (attested 2001, 2013).

Ming Mei is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MPhil from the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan. She also studied at SOAS University of London under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.

Ming-Wood Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology who earned his PhD from UCLA under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en. He studied at the University of Hong Kong and later served there as a professor (attested 1998).
Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Huifeng Shi (attested 2013).

Minori Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at Taisho University. He held positions at Taisho University, the Sanko Cultural Institute, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Minoru Hara (1930–2021) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Tokyo and Harvard. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1975–1991) and president of the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (1996–2006).
Minoru Inaba is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who served as a professor at Kyoto University (attested 2011, 2022).

Minoru Kiyota (1923–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and others. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1966–1999).

Minton Warren (1850–1907) was a linguist who studied under William Dwight Whitney at Yale and earned a Dr. phil. from Strasbourg. He held professorships at Johns Hopkins (1879–1899) and Harvard (1899), and directed the American Academy in Rome.
Minyak Kunzang Sonam was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

id: P:Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo
summary: Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
